notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware backend was run and the wire syntax was not tried on an instrument. NOT COVERED: the waveform array (the WFMPRE? preamble at tekdaq.py:205 and the IEEE 488.2 binary CURVE? block at tekdaq.py:402); the SCPI bridge moves text lines, so the package exposes the settings the clone reads and writes (CH1:SCALE?, CH2:SCALE? and the CH/TRIG/HOR writes). The card's ScpiDriver shape was kept: every command is a text line whose first token occurs in the clone. The card's entry symbol tekdaq:tds is the script's module-level VISA resource, not a class (the module defines only init, finished, writeEvent and animate, tekdaq.py:307-375); native names it and G7 checks the command mnemonics, not a class surface. The hardware backend connects to host/port (raw SCPI) or a visa_resource; the clone's serial baud rate (38400 by default, tekdaq.py:34) and the line terminator are not set by the bridge, so a deployment must configure the VISA resource. The e-stop writes ACQ:STOPA SEQ and LOC NONE (tekdaq.py:222, 321): the clone has no immediate-stop command, so this sets stop-after-sequence and releases the remote front-panel lock. site-limits.example.json is an example overlay only; the operator_required numeric writes are refused until an operator supplies the bench's bounds. No extension capability ids were used, so catalogue_requests is empty. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the check report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
